message.content: **Decision: Buy.** Microsoft's fiscal 2024 (year ended June 30, 2024) 10-K shows total revenue of **$245,122 million** (up 16% from $211,915 million), with operating income of $109,433 million (+24%), net income of $88,136 million (+22%), diluted EPS of $11.80, and operating cash flow of $118,548 million. Growth was broad-based across all three segments — Intelligent Cloud revenue rose 20% to $105,362 million (Azure and other cloud services +30%), Productivity and Business Processes rose 12% to $77,728 million, and More Personal Computing rose 13% to $62,032 million, helped by the Activision Blizzard acquisition (closed October 13, 2023, $75.4 billion) and Microsoft Cloud revenue of $137.4 billion (+23%). The balance sheet remains strong ($75.5 billion in cash and short-term investments, AAA-rated long-term debt), and the company returned $22.3 billion in dividends plus $12.0 billion of buybacks. Risks noted in the filing include heavy AI/datacenter capex ($44.5 billion of property additions), margin pressure from AI infrastructure, and the IRS's proposed $28.9 billion transfer-pricing adjustment, but none of these undermine the fundamental picture. With the quote at $420.18 (bid $420.16 / ask $420.20), I placed one limit buy order for **23 shares of MSFT at $420.50** — a limit essentially at the market — which filled at $420.50 for a total of **$9,671.50**, within the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps, using existing cash and moving no money out of the account. The account now holds 123 shares of MSFT. The key figure cited in the order's key_figures is Microsoft's fiscal 2024 total revenue of $245,122 million (USD millions), as reported in the 10-K filed July 30, 2024.
